conf.description: crowdstrike-falcon, detection-summary dataset, syslog-leef format: split the LEEF 1.0 pipe-delimited header, tokenize the tab-delimited attribute body into the crowdstrike.falcon.* namespace by literal key (no public leef.cfg attribute inventory exists), tag event.dataset.

conf.comment: crowdstrike-falcon / detection-summary / syslog-leef. The connector's cs.falconhoseclient.leef.cfg template is the authoritative attribute map but its per-attribute keys are not published anywhere reachable, so this pipeline does NOT guess an ECS mapping: it splits the LEEF header for eventType/vendor/product/version, then tokenizes the tab-delimited body and lands every attribute under crowdstrike.falcon.<literal-key> using its own on-wire name. Real per-attribute ECS mapping is a gap pending a read of the on-host leef.cfg -- see README.

functions.description: record why attribute-level ECS mapping is not attempted
split the LEEF:1.0|vendor|product|version|eventType| header from the tab-delimited attribute body

conf.code: var body = __e['attrs'] || ''; var parts = body.split(String.fromCharCode(9)); for (var i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) { var eq = parts[i].indexOf('='); if (eq > 0) { var k = parts[i].substring(0, eq).trim(); var v = parts[i].substring(eq + 1); if (k.length > 0) { __e['crowdstrike.falcon.' + k] = v; } } }

functions.description: tokenize the tab-delimited LEEF attribute body into crowdstrike.falcon.<literal-key>; code (not rename) because the key set is unsourced and not knowable in a conf
batch-rename the LEEF header capture groups into the custom namespace
tag the dataset and drop the working/raw fields now that every attribute has been extracted
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
